commentary.executiveSummary: MacWest recorded a net loss of GH¢ 12.69M in Q2 2026 (Apr–Jun), a sharp reversal from Q1 2026's marginal profit of GH¢ 0.16M. Revenue grew to GH¢ 15.60M (up 22.6% from GH¢ 12.73M in Q1), but direct costs ballooned to GH¢ 26.90M, producing a gross loss of GH¢ 11.30M vs a gross profit of GH¢ 4.33M in Q1. The H1 2026 cumulative net loss stands at GH¢ 12.53M. Cash reserves fell from GH¢ 5.76M (Q1) to GH¢ 0.83M by 30 June. Borrowings reached GH¢ 18.18M and equity turned negative at -GH¢ 6.84M. Immediate cost control, project margin recovery, and working capital management are critical priorities.
commentary.pnlAnalysis: Q2 2026 revenue grew 22.6% quarter-on-quarter to GH¢ 15.60M, reflecting sustained operational capacity. However, direct costs of GH¢ 26.90M exceeded revenue by 72.4%, eroding Q1's gross profit of GH¢ 4.33M and driving a gross loss of GH¢ 11.30M. Operating expenses rose to GH¢ 5.01M (from GH¢ 4.14M in Q1). The Q2 net loss of GH¢ 12.69M brought the H1 cumulative loss to GH¢ 12.53M, partially offset by a deferred tax credit of GH¢ 3.96M at the half-year level.
commentary.balanceSheetAnalysis: The balance sheet deteriorated significantly in Q2. Total assets held at GH¢ 18.93M while current liabilities surged to GH¢ 29.57M, driven by GH¢ 18.18M in borrowings. Equity turned negative at -GH¢ 6.84M (from +GH¢ 3.53M at Q1 2026). Cash and bank dropped 85.5% from GH¢ 5.76M (Q1) to GH¢ 0.83M. The company urgently needs to improve collections, reduce borrowings, recover project costs, and restore positive equity.

risks.description: Total equity of -GH¢ 6.84M places the company in a technically insolvent position. Immediate recapitalisation or a restructuring of the borrowing profile is required.
Cash balance of GH¢ 0.83M against GH¢ 29.57M in current liabilities represents a severe liquidity constraint. Borrowings of GH¢ 18.18M are the primary driver.
Negative gross margin of -72.4% in Q2 (vs +34.0% in Q1) indicates project costs spiralled. Urgent renegotiation of contracts and tighter cost controls are necessary.
H1 2026 revenue of GH¢ 28.33M represents only 20.6% of the GH¢ 137M annual budget. Q2 revenue of GH¢ 15.60M, while up 22.6% from Q1, is still well below the run-rate needed to close the gap.
